name: Smith Ranch Apartments
award: 2022 Federal 4% and state housing tax credits (Round Two)
headline: Smith Ranch Apartments is a 65-home, three-story tax-credit building for households at 30% to 60% AMI on town-owned land in Silverthorne's Smith Ranch neighborhood; Gorman & Company won 2022 Round Two federal 4% and $300,000 state credits for it, and residents were moving in by early 2025.
why_it_matters: It shows a mountain-town template: the Town of Silverthorne ground-leased the land, lent $1.625M and waived taps and permit fees (about $4.65M in all by the developer's count), and Gorman paired the 65 LIHTC units with 70 unsubsidized 80-120% AMI rentals built next door.

status.label: Built and leasing (move-ins under way by February 2025)
status.detail: Summit Daily reported on 2025-02-06 that move-ins had started and the 65 LIHTC units were about half leased. No public 8609 or placed-in-service date was found.

next_step: Watch for the deal on CHFA's 4% completed-developments (8609) list and for a full-occupancy report on the LIHTC building.

key_numbers.meaning: 60 units at 60% AMI, 4 at 30% AMI and one manager unit.
Plus $300,000 of state credit; CHFA issued $14,264,000 in tax-exempt bonds.
Sources: $8.4M first mortgage, about $14M credit equity, $3.9M-$4M state Division of Housing, $1.625M town loan, about $1.5M deferred fee.
Subordinate loan, tap-fee and permit-fee waivers, and a below-market ground lease, about $71,000 per unit by the application's count.

facts.value: One three-story, wood-frame, slab-on-grade walk-up building with surface parking (114 spaces in the application); NGBS 2020 Bronze target
1BR about 554 sq ft, 2BR about 757 sq ft, 3BR about 1,013 sq ft
Summit County difficult development area (DDA); next to a Summit Stage free-bus stop
Described as perpetually affordable in the application
70 deed-restricted rentals at 80%, 100% and 120% AMI in two other buildings (135 homes in all), funded without tax credits

money.note: The application said this was $4,615 per unit.

Application: plus a $2,650,000 taxable tail ($16,914,000 construction financing), private placement; Citi Community Capital named as construction and permanent lender at application. Whose bond cap was used is not stated.
Lender not named in the 2023 sources.

money.source: Federal and state tax credit equity
money.note: National Equity Fund gave a letter of interest at application; the closed investor is not named publicly.
Town also waived about $869,000 in tap fees and leased the land (land value estimated at $2M by Summit Daily).
About 45% of the fee, repaid over 15 years per the application.
Through the Summit Combined Housing Authority, per the application.

parties.name: Gorman & Company, LLC

parties.role: Landowner and ground lessor; subordinate lender
parties.name: Town of Silverthorne

background.text: Silverthorne bought the 51-acre Smith Ranch site in 2008 for about $3.5 million, using money from Summit County's 2006 ballot measure 5A; the neighborhood already had 164 deed-restricted for-sale homes at 80-120% AMI when Gorman applied, leaving no rentals for 30-60% AMI households.

The application cited the coming loss of Blue River Apartments (78 LIHTC units built in 1994), whose extended-use period was set to expire at the end of 2024 with the owner planning to convert to market rate.
Gorman held a public hearing on 2022-06-22 on its state credit and Division of Housing applications (no one attended) and presented the project to Town Council in June 2022.
CHFA's market analyst flagged a 31% capture rate (above the 25% guideline); Gorman also asked for a waiver of CHFA's cost-basis limit because of high mountain construction costs.
Silverthorne Town Council gave unanimous final approval to the 135-unit rental project on 2023-02-22; the resolution number was not found.
The workforce side (70 units, about $33.7M) used a $19.4M first mortgage, about $4.9M investor equity, subordinate loans and $3M developer equity, kept separate from the LIHTC deal.
Applications opened in November 2024: the LIHTC units first come, first served, the workforce units by lottery.

pictures.title: Smith Ranch neighborhood site plan marking the LIHTC and workforce buildings

discrepancies.text: Gorman's 2023 presentation lists the state Division of Housing loan as $3,900,000, while the 2023 trade case study gives $4 million.

In March 2023 Summit Daily said construction could start as soon as May 2023 and finish in early 2025; later Summit Daily articles say construction began in 2017, which refers to the wider neighborhood rather than this building.

open_questions: Bond closing date, the closed equity investor and credit price, and the final first-mortgage lender.
Ground lease term and rent, and the Town resolution numbers for the lease and $1.625M loan.
Placed-in-service date and 8609 issuance; current occupancy of the LIHTC building.
Whether Deneuve Construction remained the general contractor.
Whether any units carry project-based vouchers (none mentioned).
